notes: D1-RERUN-CHANCE says 6 BASE/RAW readers died after the write, before the hand-back; the transcripts show 4 (RAW-A r2, RAW-B r0, r1, r2), and the other 8 handed back normally. The record miscounts, but no answer is affected: all 12 wrote complete answers identical to their transcript payloads.

The RAW arms have no working attention control. Canary namings were 0 for all 6 RAW readers (the canary is not legible in the RAW display either), and RAW readers spent less time before writing (median 56 s from first read to write, vs 91 s for BASE and 98-142 s for REF). Their attention rests only on each having read all 15 images once. This does not invalidate the result: RAW slab AUC is near chance (pooled 0.526/0.502; per-window display 0.46-0.62) and RAW correlation with the reference is about 0.
S' = 20 sits exactly on the VOID boundary. It re-derives exactly and is stable over consensus radii 140-160 px (tightest group 64 px inside the radius), so it is robust.
The v1 display set was built before DECL-D1-A6 and withdrawn unread; no agent read a v1 image. Masking hides no sealed letter: 0 of 20 seal letters lie within 100 canvas px of a masked pixel.

The J5 BASE-fwd label-AUC peak sits at (-8, +20) display px, but the BASE-vs-REF0 cross-correlation peaks at (0, +4) display px, so this is label noise, not a frame shift. It would not matter at R 250 canvas px and is moot with 0 namings.

By design, REF0 readers see pixel-identical images to the sealers', so REF recall measures fresh-reader agreement on the same display rather than recovery from an independent source. This is the declared calibration, not a frame error, and it cannot change FAIL.
